blocks.h: 1. Why NOx forms, and the three levers every measure pulls

blocks.p: Every measure in this question is an attack on one of three things, so it is worth thirty seconds establishing them before the limbs.

ul: The nitrogen comes overwhelmingly from the air, not from the fuel. Residual fuel contains some fuel-bound nitrogen, but the great bulk of the oxides of nitrogen leaving a marine diesel engine is thermal NOx, formed from atmospheric nitrogen and oxygen in the flame. That is why NOx cannot be dealt with by buying a cleaner fuel, as sulphur can.
The formation rate rises very steeply with peak flame temperature, and requires available oxygen and time spent at that temperature.

blocks.p: So there are exactly three levers:

ul: Peak temperature - add something that absorbs heat or raises the charge's specific heat;
Oxygen availability - displace part of the oxygen with inert gas;
Residence time - shorten the time at peak, through injection timing and rate shaping.

blocks.p: And one trade-off governs the whole subject: NOx and fuel consumption pull against each other. Cooling or slowing the burn reduces NOx and costs efficiency. That is why regulation sets a ceiling rather than demanding the cleanest possible engine, and why the strictest ceiling is applied only where it is most needed.

blocks.h: (a) Tier II and Tier III emission regulation on the main engine
2. The regulatory frame - regulation 13 and what fixes the tier

blocks.p: The controlling provision is MARPOL Annex VI regulation 13. At this sitting the applicable text is the revised Annex VI introduced by resolution MEPC.328(76), which entered into force on 1 November 2022.

ul: Regulation 13 sets three tiers of permitted NOx emission for marine diesel engines above a defined power output.

Each tier's limit is not a single number - it is a function of the engine's rated speed, expressed in grammes per kilowatt-hour. A slow-speed two-stroke and a high-speed auxiliary are therefore held to different figures within the same tier. No limit value is quoted here.

Certification is under the NOx Technical Code 2008 as revised, on the test bed and by the approved methods; in-service compliance is demonstrated through the engine's NOx Technical File and its record book of parameter changes.
Certain engines are excluded - emergency engines, and engines fitted in lifeboats and survival craft.

blocks.h: 3. Tier II and Tier III - what fixes each, and the two operating modes

blocks.p: Two different things fix the two tiers, and that is the substance of this limb.

ul: The construction date of the ship fixes which tier the engine must be certified to. An engine on a ship built from the Tier II date onwards must meet Tier II; an engine on a ship built from the Tier III date onwards must additionally be capable of Tier III. It is the ship's date, not the engine's technology, that creates the obligation.

Geography fixes whether the strictest tier actually applies at any moment. Tier III is required only when the ship is operating inside a designated emission control area for NOx; outside it, the same engine may run to Tier II.

blocks.p: The practical consequence is that such a ship has two operating modes, and the change between them must be recorded - the date, the time and the ship's position on entering and on leaving. That log entry is the first thing a port State inspector asks for.

The engineering consequence is the point worth making. Tier II is reachable by combustion tuning and engine design - injection timing, chamber geometry, charging. Tier III is a step change and is not reachable by tuning alone. It requires either a heavy primary measure such as exhaust gas recirculation, or a secondary measure such as selective catalytic reduction. That is exactly why limbs (b), (c) and (d) of this question exist.

blocks.h: (b) Primary NOx reduction vis-a-vis secondary NOx reduction measures
4. Primary measures - preventing the NOx from forming

blocks.p: Definition first, because the definition is the mark. A primary measure acts on or before combustion, so that less NOx is ever created.

ul: The combustion event - retarded injection timing, the simplest measure of all and the one that costs fuel most directly; injection pressure and rate shaping; common rail, which decouples timing and pressure from engine speed and load.
The charge - Miller timing combined with high-pressure turbocharging, so that the charge expands and cools before compression begins.
Design - combustion chamber and nozzle geometry, swirl, compression ratio: designed in, not added on.
Adding water - fuel-water emulsion, direct water injection, and scavenge air moistening (limb (d)).
Changing the charge itself - exhaust gas recirculation (limb (d)).

blocks.h: 5. Secondary measures, and the comparison the limb asks for

blocks.p: A secondary measure leaves the combustion untouched and treats the exhaust. Selective catalytic reduction is the only mature secondary NOx measure in marine use - it is limb (c) and is dealt with there.
The comparison the limb asks for, on six axes:

rows: Where it acts
On or before combustion
On the exhaust, after combustion
Effect on the engine
Changes how it burns - a fuel penalty on most measures
None - the engine burns as designed
Plant required
None, or modest and largely integral
A large installation - reactor, dosing, tank
Consumables
Fresh water on the water-based measures
A reagent, with a bunkering chain behind it
Reach
Tier II readily; the strictest tier only with a heavy measure
Capable of the strictest tier
Failure mode
Degrades gradually as tuning drifts
Can fail as a system and lose the whole benefit at once

blocks.p: Three points finish the limb:

ul: The dividing line is where the NOx goes, not where the equipment sits. Ask only whether the pollutant was prevented or removed.

Which is why exhaust gas recirculation is a PRIMARY measure. Its gas comes from the exhaust, so it is constantly misclassified - but it is returned to the cylinder to change the combustion, and the NOx is never formed. This is the single commonest error on this question.
An exhaust gas scrubber is not a NOx measure at all. It addresses sulphur oxides and particulates. Introducing it here loses marks rather than gaining them.
They are complements, not rivals. Primary measures are cumulative and are used together to meet the ordinary limit; a heavy primary measure or a secondary one is added to reach the strictest.

blocks.h: 6. SCR - the reaction, and the arrangement that delivers it

blocks.p: Selective catalytic reduction converts the oxides of nitrogen already formed into harmless products before they leave the funnel.

ul: A reagent - in marine practice an aqueous urea solution, or ammonia - is injected into the exhaust upstream of a catalyst.
Urea decomposes in the hot gas to ammonia, which over the catalyst reacts selectively with the oxides of nitrogen to give nitrogen and water vapour.
'Selective' means the reagent reacts preferentially with NOx rather than being burnt by the oxygen also present in the exhaust - which is what makes the process work in a lean exhaust at all.

The installation is a reactor containing the catalyst elements, a dosing and injection system, a mixing length upstream of the reactor, a reagent storage tank and its supply and heating arrangements, plus soot blowing to keep the elements clear.

blocks.p: The reactor may sit before or after the turbocharger turbine, and which it is depends on the engine. A slow-speed two-stroke has a comparatively cool exhaust after the turbine, so the reactor is commonly placed on the high-pressure side, before the turbine, where the gas is hot enough. A four-stroke medium-speed engine generally runs hot enough after the turbine for a low-pressure arrangement, which is mechanically simpler.

blocks.h: 7. SCR - the operating window, and what it costs

blocks.p: The whole difficulty of SCR is that it only works inside a window.

ul: Temperature-sensitive. Below the window the reaction slows and stops; above it the catalyst degrades. This is precisely what decides the reactor's position relative to the turbine, and it is why low load, manoeuvring and port operation are the hard cases rather than full-away.
Sulphur-sensitive. Sulphur compounds in the exhaust form ammonium salts at low temperature that deposit on and blind the catalyst. A higher-sulphur fuel raises the minimum working temperature.

Dosing must be correct. Under-dose and NOx passes through untreated; over-dose and unreacted ammonia passes through as ammonia slip, which is itself a pollutant and is smelt long before it is measured.
It adds exhaust back pressure, which costs some engine efficiency.

It is a large installation with a consumable behind it - space and weight for the reactor and the urea tank, and a reagent bunkering chain that must be available wherever the ship trades. On a retrofit these are usually the binding constraints, not the chemistry.

blocks.p: Set against that: no fuel penalty, since the engine is untouched, and it is the route by which most large two-stroke engines meet the strictest tier.

blocks.h: (d) Scavenge Air Moisturizing and Exhaust Gas Recirculation for the main engine

blocks.p: The paper prints 'Moisturizing'; the industry term is scavenge air moistening, abbreviated SAM. It is the same system.
Water is evaporated into the scavenge air, downstream of the charge air cooler, so that the air entering the cylinder is saturated with water vapour.

ul: How it works - one lever, pulled twice. The water absorbs latent heat as it evaporates, and the resulting water vapour has a higher specific heat than the air it replaces. Both effects lower the peak combustion temperature, and NOx falls steeply with it. SAM pulls the temperature lever only.

Arrangement. A humidification section after the air cooler, often in stages with re-heating between them so that the air can carry more vapour; a water supply, circulating pump and treatment plant; and controls linked to engine load.
The water must be fresh and clean. What reaches the cylinder must not carry salt or solids - sea water would be ruinous to the liner and the valves.
A water mist catcher is the safety-critical item. The cylinder must receive vapour, never droplets: liquid water reaching a hot liner causes thermal shock and washes away the oil film.

Costs. Corrosion in the air path, disturbance to cylinder lubrication and hence to the scrape-down oil condition, a continuous fresh-water demand, a small efficiency penalty and added control complexity.

blocks.p: It is a substantial primary measure, but it is normally part of a package rather than a complete answer to the strictest tier on its own.

blocks.h: 9. Exhaust Gas Recirculation, and why both of these are primary

blocks.p: Part of the exhaust is cleaned, cooled and returned to the scavenge air.

ul: How it works - two levers at once, which is why it reaches further than SAM. The returned gas has already had its oxygen consumed, so it reduces the oxygen concentration of the charge; and the carbon dioxide and water vapour it contains raise the charge's specific heat, lowering the peak temperature. Oxygen and temperature together.

Arrangement. A scrubber to wash soot and sulphur compounds out of the recirculated gas, a cooler, a water mist catcher, an EGR blower to overcome the pressure difference, and shut-off and change-over valves so the system can be cut in and out with the tier mode.
The turbocharging must be arranged to suit - cylinder cut-out, variable geometry or auxiliary blowers - because gas is being diverted away from the turbine.
The bleed-off water is a waste stream in its own right. It is acidic and carries soot and metals, and it must be treated, held and monitored against the discharge criteria before any release.
Costs. Fouling and acid corrosion in the gas path, soot carried into the cylinder, blower power, considerable complexity, and the waste-water handling above.

blocks.p: EGR is capable of reaching the strictest tier on its own, and it is the principal primary alternative to SCR for large two-strokes.

Close the limb on the classification, because it is where the marks are lost. Both SAM and EGR are PRIMARY measures. In both, the combustion itself is altered and the NOx is never formed. Neither treats the exhaust on its way out - EGR takes gas from the exhaust, but it sends it back into the engine to change the burn, and that is what puts it on the primary side of the line drawn in limb (b).

Four limbs at four marks each means four short, complete answers - not one long answer and three notes. The opening mechanism section is what makes that possible: once the three levers are established, each limb can be written in a few lines without becoming thin, because the reader already has the physics.

Within limb (b) the six-axis table does the comparison the word vis-a-vis asks for. A candidate who describes primary measures and then describes secondary measures, without ever comparing them, has answered a different question.

ul: Calling exhaust gas recirculation a secondary measure. The single most common error on this question. Its gas comes from the exhaust, but it goes back into the cylinder to change the combustion, so the NOx is never formed.
Bringing in the exhaust gas scrubber. That is a sulphur and particulate device. It is not a NOx measure.
Quoting tier limit values. They are a function of rated speed, so a single number is wrong. Explain the structure instead.
Saying Tier III applies from a date. The date fixes what the engine must be CAPABLE of; geography fixes when it must actually deliver it.
Writing limbs (b) and (d) at eight-mark length. Earlier sittings paid eight for that material; this one pays four.
Forgetting the water mist catcher on SAM, which is the item that keeps liquid water out of the cylinder.
'Tier 2 and 3' is printed in arabic numerals where the Annex uses roman. Nothing turns on it.
'Moisturizing' is the paper's spelling. The system is scavenge air moistening. Note it once and move on; do not lecture the examiner.
'Primary' does not mean 'first' or 'main'. It means the measure acts before or during combustion. A candidate who reads it as 'the principal measures' will build the whole limb wrongly.
SCR's position relative to the turbine is not a fixed fact - it depends on the exhaust temperature the engine delivers. Explain the dependence rather than asserting one arrangement.
Ammonia slip is a consequence of over-dosing, not of the catalyst failing.
The tier changeover must be logged with date, time and position. That operational detail is worth a mark and is regularly omitted.
Your SCR is fitted and the ship is manoeuvring in an ECA at low load. What is your concern?
Why does higher-sulphur fuel raise the minimum working temperature of an SCR?
What would happen if the water mist catcher on a SAM plant failed?
Where does the bleed-off water from an EGR scrubber go?
Why does retarding the injection reduce NOx, and what does it cost you?
Your ship is Tier III capable by EGR. What do you do on entering an ECA, and what do you write down?
Can you meet Tier III by tuning alone?

blocks.p: Set up three levers at the start - TEMPERATURE, OXYGEN, TIME - and every limb afterwards is a sentence about which lever is being pulled:

ul: SAM - temperature only, by latent heat and specific heat.
EGR - temperature and oxygen. Two levers, so it reaches further.
Retarded timing and rate shaping - temperature and residence time.
SCR - no lever at all. It does not prevent the NOx; it removes it afterwards. That is the whole of the primary/secondary divide.

blocks.p: And for the tiers: the date says what the engine must be able to do; the chart says when it must do it.

blocks.p: MARPOL Annex VI is held by the True Source corpus, but its corpus classification is citation-ready only - it resolves to instrument identity and provenance and not to text. Regulation 13 is therefore given by identity and effect, and no tier limit value is quoted anywhere in this answer. That restriction is also a temporal safeguard: it makes it impossible to import a limit from a consolidated text later than this sitting.

A known defect in the corpus amendment register is declared here rather than relied on. The register records the entry into force of the revised Annex VI as 1 November 2023. That is four months after this sitting, and taken at face value it would force this answer onto a superseded Annex. The correct date is 1 November 2022, from the resolution's own operative provisions. The register entry is a known corpus correction request already raised by an earlier paper; it is not repaired from this branch, because question production never edits True Source.

One later amendment is excluded deliberately. Resolution MEPC.385(81) was adopted in March 2024 and replaced the major-conversion provision of regulation 13. Any consolidated Annex VI text dated 1 May 2024 or later incorporates it. It is future by eight months at this sitting and is not relied on; and this is why the July 2024 question on the same subject was consumed for its technical content only, with its regulatory currency statement re-derived from the July 2023 position.
No emission control area is named and no area is asserted to have been designated for NOx at any particular date. The concept is used; the geography is not.

questions.recurrence_adjudication: Adjudicated by reading four printed stems - this one, QP2303-Q4, QP2310-Q5 and QP2407-Q9. The opening sentence recurs character-identically across three 2023 sittings, and every one of this question's four limbs recurs somewhere in the corpus, but NO SINGLE QUESTION CARRIES ALL FOUR. Recorded as PARTIAL: an examiner reassembly of two previously separate questions under one stem, not a recurrence of either.

blocks.p: Burning fuel in air makes an oxide of nitrogen that nobody wants, and the awkward part is that the nitrogen mostly comes out of the air itself, not out of the fuel. So you cannot fix it by buying cleaner fuel, the way you fix sulphur. Nitrogen and oxygen are perfectly happy sitting next to each other until the flame gets hot enough to force them together, and the hotter the flame the more of it you get - not gently, but very sharply indeed.

That single fact organises the whole question. If heat is what makes it, then anything that takes the peak temperature down will make less of it: put water in, because water soaks up heat when it evaporates; open the valves at a different moment so the burn is spread out; let the charge expand and cool before you squeeze it. And if oxygen is the other half of the reaction, then diluting the oxygen works too - which is what feeding some of the used exhaust back into the engine achieves, since that gas has already had its oxygen burnt out of it.

Everything above happens inside the engine and stops the stuff being made. There is a completely different approach: let the engine burn however it likes, and clean the exhaust afterwards by squirting in a chemical that turns the oxide back into ordinary nitrogen and water over a catalyst. That is the whole of the divide the second limb asks about - before or after. It is not about where the equipment is bolted; it is about whether the pollutant is prevented or removed.

The catch that makes it an engineering problem rather than a solved one: the settings that make an engine clean generally make it thirstier. Cooling the flame costs efficiency. So the rules do not ask for the cleanest possible engine - they set a ceiling, make the ceiling depend on how fast the engine runs, and make the strictest ceiling apply only in the places that need it most. Which is why a ship can have two ways of running and switch between them at a line on the chart.

decomposition_gate.question_intent: Four short-note limbs at four marks each, on one subject. The examiner is testing breadth and precision rather than depth: he wants each limb answered correctly and briefly, and he has arranged them so that limbs a) and c) are recall and limbs b) and d) are understanding. The single discriminating judgement on the whole question is whether the candidate places EXHAUST GAS RECIRCULATION on the correct side of the primary/secondary divide - it is PRIMARY, and calling it secondary because the gas comes from the exhaust is the standard error.

Second, MEPC.385(81) was adopted in March 2024 and any consolidated Annex VI text of 1 May 2024 or later incorporates it - so the July 2024 donor's regulatory statement is contaminated and was not carried.
decomposition_gate.jurisdiction_risk: LOW - MARPOL Annex VI applies through the flag State without Indian modification for this purpose. No Indian statutory limb is asserted, so the Merchant Shipping Act contamination risk does not arise on this question. Emission control areas are named as a concept; no individual area is asserted to have been designated at any particular date.
decomposition_gate.technical_ambiguities: The paper prints 'Scavenge Air Moisturizing'; the industry term is scavenge air MOISTENING. The printed form is preserved in text_verbatim and the correct term is given once in the answer, without suggesting the examiner is wrong. 'Tier 2 and 3' is printed in arabic numerals where the Annex uses roman; both are used and no distinction is drawn. 'for ME' is the paper's abbreviation for the main engine. SCR's position relative to the turbine depends on engine type and exhaust temperature; the answer explains the dependence rather than asserting one arrangement.
decomposition_gate.target_answer_shape: Nine numbered sections under four single-letter limb headings, opening with a short mechanism section that every limb afterwards draws on. Limb a) two sections; limb b) two; limb c) two; limb d) two. The mechanism section is what allows the four limbs to be short without being thin.

steps.title: Why NOx forms, and the three levers every measure pulls
points: The nitrogen comes overwhelmingly from the AIR, not from the fuel - so it cannot be fixed by changing fuel
Formation rate rises VERY STEEPLY with peak flame temperature, and needs available oxygen and time at that temperature
Three levers follow: PEAK TEMPERATURE, OXYGEN AVAILABILITY, RESIDENCE TIME. The governing trade-off is that NOx and fuel consumption pull against each other

steps.title: The regulatory frame - regulation 13 and what fixes the tier
points: MARPOL Annex VI regulation 13; at this sitting the REVISED Annex VI introduced by MEPC.328(76), in force 1 November 2022
Three tiers; each tier's limit is a FUNCTION OF THE ENGINE'S RATED SPEED, not a single number

An output threshold applies and certain emergency and survival-craft engines are excluded; certification under the NOx Technical Code 2008 as revised, with in-service compliance through the NOx Technical File

steps.title: Tier II and Tier III - what fixes each, and the two operating modes
points: The CONSTRUCTION DATE fixes which tier the engine must meet - this is the point of the limb
TIER II is the global standard for the modern engine and is reachable by combustion tuning and engine design

TIER III applies ADDITIONALLY when operating in a designated emission control area for NOx - so a ship has TWO OPERATING MODES, and the changeover is recorded with date, time and position. Tier III is a STEP CHANGE and is not reachable by tuning alone

steps.title: Primary measures - preventing the NOx from forming
points: Definition: the measure acts ON OR BEFORE COMBUSTION so that LESS NOx IS EVER CREATED

Combustion event - retarded injection timing, injection pressure and rate shaping, common rail; design - chamber and nozzle geometry, swirl, compression ratio; Miller timing with high-pressure charging
Adding water - fuel-water emulsion, direct water injection, scavenge air moistening; changing the charge - exhaust gas recirculation

steps.title: Secondary measures, and the comparison the limb asks for
points: Definition: combustion is LEFT UNTOUCHED and the EXHAUST IS TREATED. SCR is the only mature secondary measure in marine use
Compare on: where it acts, effect on the engine, plant required, consumables, reach, failure mode. Primary costs FUEL; secondary costs PLANT AND A CONSUMABLE but no fuel penalty
THE DIVIDING LINE IS WHERE THE NOx GOES, NOT WHERE THE EQUIPMENT SITS - which is why EGR is PRIMARY. An exhaust gas scrubber is not a NOx measure at all. The two families are complements, not rivals

steps.title: SCR - the reaction, and the arrangement that delivers it
points: A reagent - aqueous urea or ammonia - is injected into the exhaust upstream of a catalyst
Over the catalyst the NOx and the reagent react to NITROGEN AND WATER, both harmless
Reactor, dosing system, mixing length, reagent tank and supply; the reactor sits BEFORE or AFTER the turbine depending on the exhaust temperature the engine gives

steps.title: SCR - the operating window, and what it costs
points: TEMPERATURE-SENSITIVE: too cold and the reaction stops and salts form; too hot and the catalyst degrades. This is what decides the reactor's position
SULPHUR-SENSITIVE: sulphur compounds form salts at low temperature that blind the catalyst. Low-load and manoeuvring operation is the difficult case

Dosing must be right or unreacted reagent passes through as AMMONIA SLIP; and it adds exhaust back pressure, a large installation, a consumable and a bunkering chain. It is the route by which most large two-stroke engines reach the strictest tier

steps.title: Scavenge Air Moisturizing
points: Water is EVAPORATED INTO THE SCAVENGE AIR downstream of the charge air cooler - vapour into the cylinder, never droplets
Latent heat absorbed on evaporation plus water vapour's higher specific heat: BOTH lower the peak temperature. It pulls the TEMPERATURE lever only

Humidification section, water treatment - what reaches the cylinder must be fresh and clean - and a WATER MIST CATCHER, the safety-critical item. Costs: corrosion, disturbed cylinder lubrication, fresh water demand, a small efficiency penalty

steps.title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation, and why both of these are primary
points: Part of the exhaust is CLEANED, COOLED AND RETURNED to the scavenge air: scrubber, cooler, water mist catcher, EGR blower, shut-off and change-over valves
It pulls TWO LEVERS AT ONCE - it reduces the oxygen concentration of the charge AND raises its specific heat through carbon dioxide and water vapour - which is why it reaches further than SAM

Costs: fouling, acid corrosion, soot into the cylinder, blower power, and acidic bleed-off water requiring treatment and monitoring. BOTH SAM AND EGR ARE PRIMARY, because in both the NOx is never formed

questions.memory_cue: Three levers - TEMPERATURE, OXYGEN, TIME - set up at step 1 and every limb hangs off them. SAM pulls temperature (8). EGR pulls temperature AND oxygen (9). SCR pulls neither: it cleans up afterwards (6-7). Tiers say how far you must pull (2-3).

quick_revision.recall_15s: NOx IS THERMAL - the nitrogen comes from the AIR, so a cleaner fuel does not help. THREE LEVERS: peak temperature, oxygen availability, residence time. Governing trade-off: NOx and fuel consumption pull against each other. (a) MARPOL ANNEX VI REGULATION 13, revised Annex VI per MEPC.328(76) IN FORCE 1 NOVEMBER 2022. Three tiers; each tier's limit is a FUNCTION OF RATED SPEED, not one number. CONSTRUCTION DATE fixes which tier the engine must meet; GEOGRAPHY - operation inside a NOx emission control area - fixes when Tier III must actually be delivered. Two operating modes, changeover LOGGED WITH DATE, TIME AND POSITION. Certification under the NOx Technical Code 2008 as revised; in service through the NOx Technical File. Tier II by tuning and design; TIER III IS A STEP CHANGE and needs EGR or SCR. (b) PRIMARY acts ON OR BEFORE COMBUSTION so LESS NOx IS EVER CREATED - retarded timing, rate shaping, common rail, Miller timing, chamber and nozzle design, water emulsion, direct water injection, SAM, EGR. SECONDARY leaves combustion alone and TREATS THE EXHAUST - SCR is the only mature marine one. Primary costs FUEL and degrades gradually; secondary costs PLANT AND A REAGENT and can fail as a system. THE LINE IS WHERE THE NOx GOES, NOT WHERE THE PLANT SITS - so EGR IS PRIMARY. A scrubber is not a NOx measure. (c) SCR - urea or ammonia injected upstream of a catalyst; NOx and reagent react SELECTIVELY to NITROGEN AND WATER. Reactor before the turbine on a slow-speed two-stroke, after it on a hotter four-stroke. TEMPERATURE-SENSITIVE and SULPHUR-SENSITIVE - salts blind the catalyst at low temperature, so low load and manoeuvring are the hard cases. Over-dosing gives AMMONIA SLIP. Adds back pressure, space, weight and a bunkering chain; no fuel penalty. (d) SAM - water EVAPORATED into the scavenge air after the air cooler; latent heat plus higher specific heat; TEMPERATURE LEVER ONLY; water must be fresh and clean; WATER MIST CATCHER is safety-critical - vapour never droplets; costs corrosion, cylinder lubrication and fresh water. EGR - exhaust cleaned, cooled and returned; scrubber, cooler, mist catcher, EGR blower, change-over valves; TWO LEVERS - less oxygen AND higher specific heat - so it reaches Tier III alone; costs fouling, acid corrosion, soot, blower power and acidic bleed-off water. BOTH SAM AND EGR ARE PRIMARY.

quick_revision.critical_regulation: MARPOL Annex VI regulation 13, in the revised Annex VI introduced by MEPC.328(76) and in force from 1 November 2022, with certification under the NOx Technical Code 2008 as revised.
quick_revision.major_trap: Classifying EXHAUST GAS RECIRCULATION as a secondary measure. The gas is taken from the exhaust, which invites the error, but it is returned to the cylinder to change the combustion and the NOx is therefore NEVER FORMED - which makes it PRIMARY. The dividing line is where the NOx goes, not where the equipment sits. The second trap is importing the exhaust gas scrubber, which addresses sulphur oxides and particulates and is not a NOx measure at all.

retrieval_cards.prompt: What exactly divides a primary from a secondary NOx measure, and on which side does EGR fall?
retrieval_cards.answer: A primary measure acts on or before combustion so that less NOx is ever created; a secondary measure leaves the combustion untouched and treats the exhaust. The dividing line is where the NOx goes, not where the equipment sits. EGR is PRIMARY: its gas comes from the exhaust, but it is returned to the cylinder to alter the combustion, so the NOx is never formed.

retrieval_cards.prompt: What fixes which NOx tier an engine must meet, and what fixes when the strictest tier applies?
retrieval_cards.answer: The ship's CONSTRUCTION DATE fixes which tier the engine must be certified to. GEOGRAPHY fixes when Tier III must actually be delivered - it is required only when operating inside a designated emission control area for NOx. The ship therefore has two operating modes, and the changeover is recorded with date, time and position.

retrieval_cards.prompt: Why can you not state a Tier II or Tier III limit as a single figure?
retrieval_cards.answer: Because each tier's limit is a function of the engine's rated speed, expressed in grammes per kilowatt-hour. A slow-speed two-stroke and a high-speed auxiliary are held to different figures within the same tier. Explain the structure; do not quote a number.

retrieval_cards.prompt: How does SCR work, and what are its two sensitivities?
retrieval_cards.answer: Aqueous urea or ammonia is injected into the exhaust upstream of a catalyst; over the catalyst the reagent reacts selectively with the oxides of nitrogen to give nitrogen and water. It is TEMPERATURE-sensitive - too cold and the reaction stops, too hot and the catalyst degrades, which decides whether the reactor sits before or after the turbine - and SULPHUR-sensitive, because sulphur compounds form salts at low temperature that blind the catalyst. Low load and manoeuvring are the hard cases.

retrieval_cards.prompt: What is ammonia slip and what causes it?
retrieval_cards.answer: Unreacted reagent passing through the SCR reactor and out of the funnel as ammonia. It is caused by over-dosing - injecting more reagent than the catalyst and the available NOx can consume - not by failure of the catalyst itself.

retrieval_cards.prompt: SAM against EGR - which levers does each pull, and what does each cost?
retrieval_cards.answer: SAM pulls TEMPERATURE only, by latent heat of evaporation and by the higher specific heat of water vapour. EGR pulls TEMPERATURE AND OXYGEN, which is why it reaches further and can meet the strictest tier alone. SAM costs fresh water, corrosion and disturbed cylinder lubrication, and its critical item is the water mist catcher. EGR costs blower power, fouling, acid corrosion, soot into the cylinder and acidic bleed-off water requiring treatment.

retrieval_cards.prompt: Is an exhaust gas scrubber a NOx reduction measure?
retrieval_cards.answer: No. An exhaust gas cleaning system addresses sulphur oxides and particulates. It is not a NOx measure and introducing it into an answer on nitrogen oxides loses marks rather than gaining them.

retrieval_cards.prompt: Which text of MARPOL Annex VI is applicable at a July 2023 sitting?
retrieval_cards.answer: The revised Annex VI introduced by resolution MEPC.328(76), which entered into force on 1 NOVEMBER 2022. MEPC.385(81), adopted in March 2024, is future by eight months and does not apply; any consolidated Annex VI text dated 1 May 2024 or later incorporates it and must not be used for this sitting.

notes: THE PREFERRED DONOR RUNS BACKWARDS AND THAT IS THE SAFE DIRECTION. QP2303-Q4 is MARCH 2023, four months earlier and in the same year. An earlier donor cannot drag later law backwards, so the forward-contamination risk on limbs b) and d) is closed at source.

THE OPPOSITE RISK WAS CHECKED - AN EARLIER DONOR DOES NOT AUTOMATICALLY CONTAIN LATER DEVELOPMENTS. Between March and July 2023 the only relevant event is MEPC 80, which sat 3 to 7 July 2023. IT MADE NO AMENDMENT TO MARPOL ANNEX VI REGULATION 13. The NOx substance is therefore identical at both sittings and the donor transfers intact.

THE 7 JULY 2023 BOUNDARY TOUCHES THIS QUESTION'S CURRENCY STATEMENT, NOT ITS SUBSTANCE, AND IT HAS BEEN NEUTRALISED BY STRUCTURE. MEPC 80 sat 3 to 7 July 2023 and this paper prints no day, so ANY CLAIM ABOUT THE MOST RECENT MEPC SESSION WOULD BE DAY-DEPENDENT AND UNVERIFIABLE. THIS ANSWER MAKES NO SUCH CLAIM. It states the operative instrument - the revised Annex VI, in force 1 November 2022 - which is true on both sides of 7 July, and it relies on the separately established fact that MEPC 80 amended nothing in regulation 13. The answer is therefore correct whichever side of the boundary this sitting fell, and NO HEDGE APPEARS IN THE CANDIDATE-FACING PROSE.

THE 2023 IMO GHG STRATEGY IS NOT MENTIONED AND MUST NOT BE. It was adopted at MEPC 80 on 7 July 2023, so its availability at this sitting is day-dependent. It is also irrelevant: this is a NITROGEN OXIDES question and the Strategy is a greenhouse gas instrument. Both reasons are recorded so that a later reviewer does not add it.

THE JULY 2024 DONOR IS PARTIALLY REJECTED AND THE REASON IS SPECIFIC. QP2407-Q9 states regulation 13 as consolidated to 1 MAY 2024, which incorporates MEPC.385(81) - adopted March 2024, replacing the major-conversion provision at regulation 13.2.2, and FUTURE BY EIGHT MONTHS at this sitting. ITS TECHNICAL CONTENT ON THE TIER STRUCTURE AND ON SCR IS CARRIED; ITS REGULATORY CURRENCY STATEMENT IS NOT, and was re-derived from the July 2023 position. The October 2023 answer on the same subject declined to use it as a donor at all for the same reason.

THE CORPUS AMENDMENT REGISTER IS WRONG AND THE ERROR IS LOAD-BEARING FOR THIS SITTING. It records the entry into force of the revised Annex VI as 2023-11-01. That is FOUR MONTHS AFTER THIS SITTING and, taken at face value, would force this answer onto a superseded Annex VI. The correct date is 1 NOVEMBER 2022, from the resolution's own operative provisions. This is the standing correction request already raised by an earlier paper; IT IS NOT REPAIRED FROM THIS BRANCH, because question production never edits True Source. The correct date is used and the discrepancy is declared in the answer's uncertainty section and in the paper anchor.
NO TIER LIMIT VALUE IS QUOTED, which is a corpus-position control with a temporal effect: it removes any possibility of importing a value from a later consolidated text.

FUTURE CONTAMINATION SWEEP, RUN AND CLEAN. EU ETS application to maritime begins 1 January 2024 and is absent - it is an attractive addition to an emissions answer and is deliberately excluded. MEPC 81, 82 and 83 and the IMO Net-Zero Framework are absent. The 33rd Assembly adopted on 6 December 2023 and no A.11xx(33) instrument appears. No Indian statutory limb is asserted, so the Merchant Shipping Act 2025 contamination risk does not arise.

EEXI AND CII ARE OPERATIVE AT THIS SITTING, FROM 1 JANUARY 2023, BUT ARE NOT MENTIONED. They belong to the greenhouse gas chapter of the Annex, not to regulation 13, and importing them would blur the very distinction this question tests.

blocks.h: 1. Which text applies, and how the Convention is built

blocks.p: The Maritime Labour Convention, 2006 is an ILO instrument which entered into force on 20 August 2013 and is generally described as the fourth pillar of the international regulatory regime, alongside SOLAS, MARPOL and STCW.
Say how it is built, because all four limbs of this question sit inside that structure:

ul: Articles - the treaty obligations of the Member;
Regulations - the substantive requirements;
Code Part A - Standards, which are mandatory;
Code Part B - Guidelines, which are guidance to be given due consideration.
Five Titles, of which Title 5 is compliance and enforcement and divides into flag State, port State and labour-supplying responsibilities - the same three-way split this question follows.

blocks.p: One temporal point belongs at the top. At this sitting the operative text is the Convention as amended through the 2018 amendments. The amendments approved by the International Labour Conference at its 110th Session in 2022 are adopted but not yet in force; they enter into force on 23 December 2024. Nothing from that set is a present obligation.

blocks.h: (a) Flag State and port State responsibilities
2. Flag State and port State responsibilities

blocks.p: Flag State. The flag State must establish an effective system of inspection and certification of labour conditions, ensuring that ships flying its flag comply.

ul: It may authorise recognized organizations to carry out inspection and certification, but it remains fully responsible for the work done on its behalf, must satisfy itself of their competence and independence, and must make the list public.

Ships of 500 gross tonnage and over on international voyages, or operating from or between foreign ports, must carry a Maritime Labour Certificate and a Declaration of Maritime Labour Compliance; others may be certified on request.

The DMLC is in two parts, and the split is the classic examination point. Part I is drawn up by the competent authority and identifies the national requirements; Part II is drawn up by the shipowner and sets out the measures adopted on the ship to ensure ongoing compliance.
The certificate is valid for five years, with an intermediate inspection between the second and third anniversary dates; an interim certificate may be issued for six months.

The interval between inspections shall in no case exceed three years. Inspectors must be qualified and independent, must report to the authority and the master, and have power to require rectification and to prohibit the ship from sailing until deficiencies are put right.

blocks.p: Port State. Any foreign ship calling in the port of a Member may be inspected to determine compliance.

ul: But the certificate and the DMLC must be accepted as prima facie evidence of compliance, so the ordinary inspection is a document review. Without that presumption the certificate would be worth nothing and every port would re-audit every ship.
The port State inspection is limited to the Articles, the Regulations and Part A of the Code - the mandatory material. Part B Guidelines are not the measure of compliance.

No more favourable treatment. A ship flying the flag of a State that has not ratified the Convention is entitled to no better treatment than one that has - which is what stops non-ratification from becoming a commercial advantage.
Where more is needed, the officer proceeds to a more detailed inspection, which is limb (c).

blocks.p: Every ship must carry on-board procedures for the fair, effective and expeditious handling of seafarer complaints alleging breaches of the Convention.

ul: The design preference is resolution at the lowest level - the complaint is raised with the head of department and worked upward.

But that preference is expressly without prejudice to the seafarer's right to complain directly to the master, and to complain directly to external authorities - the flag State administration, or an authorized officer in a port of call. A procedure that required him to exhaust the chain of command first would not comply.

A copy of the procedures must be provided to every seafarer, together with contact information for the competent authority of the flag State and of the seafarer's country of residence, and the name of a person on board who can advise him impartially and otherwise assist him.
The seafarer has the right to be accompanied or represented during the procedure.
Victimization for filing a complaint is prohibited and must be penalized. This is the provision that makes everything else usable: without it the machinery exists and nobody dares use it.

blocks.p: A seafarer may bring a complaint to an authorized officer in the port at which the ship has called. The procedure is an escalation with three rungs:

ul: Ship level first. The officer makes an initial investigation, and where the complaint can be resolved at ship level he seeks that resolution - the on-board procedure is used or reinstated, and where the complaint concerns matters within a more detailed inspection he proceeds accordingly.

Flag State next. If it cannot be resolved on board, the officer notifies the flag State, seeking advice and a corrective plan of action, with a deadline. A copy of the report goes to the shipowners' and seafarers' organisations in the port State.

The ILO last. Where the matter remains unresolved, the port State sends a copy of the report, with the flag State's response, to the Director-General of the International Labour Office, so that the failure is recorded internationally.

The source of the complaint is kept confidential at every stage, and the officer must take appropriate steps to safeguard it - including giving no intimation to the master or the owner that an inspection was made on account of a complaint.

blocks.p: Begin with what the Convention does not do. Unlike the regional port State control memoranda, the MLC publishes no list of detainable deficiencies. It states two grounds, and a candidate who recites a memorandum's list has answered from the wrong instrument.
The two grounds. A ship may be detained where the conditions on board are shown, following a more detailed inspection, to be:

ul: clearly hazardous to the safety, health or security of seafarers; or
a serious or repeated breach of the requirements of the Convention, including seafarers' rights.

blocks.p: The route to them matters as much as the grounds themselves. Detention is reached only through a more detailed inspection, and that inspection may be carried out only where one of four triggers is present:

ul: the required documents are not produced, or are not maintained, or are falsely maintained, or do not contain the information required;
there are clear grounds for believing the working and living conditions do not conform;
there are reasonable grounds to believe the ship changed flag to avoid compliance;
there is a complaint alleging that specific conditions do not conform.

blocks.p: What follows a finding.

ul: The deficiencies are to be rectified; or, where rectification cannot be completed in that port, the officer may accept a plan of action with a timetable.
The ship is not released until the hazard is removed or the plan accepted.
The flag State is notified forthwith, and the shipowners' and seafarers' organisations in the port State are informed.
Compensation is payable for any loss or damage suffered where a ship is unduly detained or delayed. The burden of proof rests on the shipowner, and that provision is the discipline on the inspector.

blocks.h: (d) Grievance redressal mechanisms for Indian seafarers

blocks.p: Answer this in three layers, because a single list would hide the point.

Layer 1 - the Convention's own route, which every Indian seafarer already has. India is a ratifying Member, so the whole of the machinery in limbs (b) and (c) is available to him: the on-board procedure with its impartial adviser and its protection from victimization; direct complaint to the master; direct complaint to the flag State administration; complaint to an authorized officer in any port of a ratifying Member; and, at the end, the Director-General of the ILO.
Layer 2 - what India can actually reach, and this is the substance of the limb.

ul: For an Indian-flag ship, India is the flag State and the full inspection, certification and enforcement apparatus of Title 5 is Indian.

But most Indian seafarers serve on foreign-flag ships, where India is neither the flag State nor, usually, the port State. The operative head is then India's labour-supplying responsibility, which is the third limb of Title 5 and is the one that exists precisely for large seafarer-supplying countries.

Under it, and under the recruitment and placement provisions, India licenses and regulates crewing agents, requires registers to be kept and employment agreements to be verified, enforces the prohibition on charging recruitment fees to the seafarer - save for the statutory medical certificate, the seafarer's book and a passport - and requires a system of protection to compensate the seafarer for monetary loss arising from the agent's failure to meet its obligations.
That is where the practical remedy lies. The foreign owner is beyond India's reach; the agent who put the man on board is not.

blocks.p: Layer 3 - the domestic frame.

ul: The Merchant Shipping Act, 1958 is the statute in force, and is the vehicle through which India gives effect to its flag State, port State and labour-supplying obligations.
The shipping master is the officer concerned with engagement and discharge of seafarers and with disputes over wages arising from them.
The Directorate General of Shipping is the maritime administration and the competent authority for the purposes of the Convention.
Practical actors, but not law: the seafarers' unions, and the ITF inspectorate, which in practice recovers a great deal of unpaid wage.

blocks.p: No circular number, named cell, named office, forum or tribunal is asserted here, and no section of the 1958 Act is cited by number. The machinery above is stated at the level at which it is verifiable.

blocks.h: 7. The thread that joins the four limbs

blocks.p: Close by connecting them, because the connection is the understanding the examiner is testing.

The flag State certifies and the port State verifies - and both can be entirely satisfied while a seafarer sits unpaid on a properly certified ship. Certification catches systems; it does not catch individual wrongs. What closes that gap is the complaint - and that is exactly why a complaint is not merely a welfare mechanism but one of the four triggers that entitles an officer to stop treating the certificate as conclusive, carry out a more detailed inspection, and if necessary detain the ship.

Limb (d) is the same thread followed to its Indian end. India cannot inspect a foreign ship in a foreign port; what it can do is regulate the agent who is within its reach, and make that agent answerable for the engagement it arranged.

Four limbs at four marks each. The framing section is short and buys structure for the whole answer by establishing the Articles / Regulations / Part A / Part B architecture, which every limb afterwards uses without re-explaining.

Limb (b) is given two numbered sections because the on-board and onshore procedures are separate machinery with separate rules. Running them together is the commonest way to lose half that limb. The closing section is worth writing even under time pressure: it is where the candidate shows he understands why the pieces are arranged as they are, and it takes four lines.

ul: Reciting the Paris MoU list of detainable deficiencies. That is a different instrument. The MLC publishes no list and gives two grounds.
Saying Part I of the DMLC is drawn up by the shipowner. Part I is the competent authority's; Part II is the shipowner's.
Describing port State inspection as a full audit. The certificate is prima facie evidence; the ordinary inspection is a document review.
Treating the on-board procedure as compulsory before any external complaint. The lowest-level preference is expressly without prejudice to direct complaint to the master or to external authorities.
Answering limb (d) as though India were the flag State. For most Indian seafarers it is not; the operative head is labour-supplying responsibility.
Citing the 2022 amendments as current obligations. They enter into force 23 December 2024, seventeen months after this sitting.
Inventing an Indian forum. No cell, tribunal, circular or section number should appear.
Part B is guidance, not the measure of compliance. A port State inspection is limited to the Articles, the Regulations and Part A.
The MLC is amended by the ILO's own tripartite machinery, not by IMO tacit acceptance. Candidates habitually import the IMO procedure.
'Detainable deficiency' is port State control vocabulary. The examiner has used it; answer it with the MLC grounds and say so.
Compensation for undue detention is a real provision and is the check on the inspector. It is regularly omitted.
Confidentiality of the source runs through the whole complaint machinery, including that the master is not to be told an inspection arose from a complaint.
Victimization is prohibited AND penalized. Both words matter - a prohibition without a penalty would be decorative.
The administration at this sitting is DG Shipping. The later renaming belongs to a statute that is years away from this paper.
Who signs Part II of the DMLC, and what is in it?
A seafarer tells you he has not been paid for three months. Walk me through what happens.
On what grounds can a port State detain a ship under the MLC, and who pays if you are wrong?
Your ship changes flag in the middle of a wage dispute. Does that help the owner?
What is the difference between the MLC route to detention and the SOLAS route?
An Indian seafarer on a foreign-flag ship has been charged a fee by his agent. What can India do?
Why must the certificate be accepted as prima facie evidence at all?

blocks.p: Follow the seafarer outward, one rung at a time, and the four limbs come in the printed order:

ul: Who certifies, and who checks? - flag State and port State (limb a).
How does he complain on board? - lowest level, but direct access preserved, and no victimization (limb b, first half).
How does he complain ashore? - authorized officer, then flag State, then the ILO (limb b, second half).
When is the ship stopped? - two grounds, four triggers, one more detailed inspection (limb c).
What can India reach? - not the foreign owner; the agent (limb d).

blocks.p: One sentence ties it: certificates catch systems, complaints catch wrongs.

blocks.p: The MLC is held by the True Source corpus at commit 319524c - the base text, the ILO Compendium and the 2022 amendments. The regulation and Standard identities above and their effects are supported from that holding. No provision is quoted.

The freshness risk on this question is HIGH, and it is physical rather than theoretical. The corpus holds two consolidated texts of the Convention - one carrying the amendments through 2018, and one carrying the 2022 set - and the second is present, readable and inapplicable at this sitting. That is exactly the circumstance in which a wrong-edition answer gets written without anyone noticing. The corpus segregates the 2022 material in a not-yet-in-force folder, and that segregation is what makes the distinction safe to state.

No ratification figure is given. The corpus records a ratification count and tonnage percentage current to a date well after this sitting. That figure cannot be carried backwards and no substitute is available from a held source, so the answer says ratification is very wide and gives no number.

The Indian limb has no held primary source. The Merchant Shipping Act, 1958 is not held by the corpus, which holds the 2025 Act - future by roughly thirty-two months at this sitting. Everything in Layer 3 is therefore authoritative secondary, stated at the level of institutional identity, and no section number, circular number, named cell, office, forum or tribunal is asserted.

questions.recurrence_adjudication: Adjudicated by reading both printed stems in full. The four limbs are the same, in the same order, in the same words, with two differences: this sitting prints COMPLAINT where February prints Compliant, and this sitting prints a mark figure against each limb where February prints none. Recorded as NEAR rather than EXACT because a corrected word and an added mark allocation are both real differences to a candidate, and because the direction matters - the later sitting is the one that prints the intended word, which is worth recording so that a future reader does not assume the July copy has been silently tidied.

blocks.p: A seafarer's problem is that the people who owe him things are a long way away and the ship keeps moving. His employer may be registered in one country, the ship flagged in a second, the crew agent in a third, and he himself may be in a port belonging to none of them. So the Convention that protects him is built to answer one question over and over: when this man has a grievance, who can actually do something about it, and can he reach them?
The design is layered, and the four parts of this question are simply four layers of the same structure.

First, the flag State - the country whose flag the ship flies - has to run a real system of checking and certifying, and the ship carries paper saying it passed. Second, any port she visits may look at her too, and the visiting inspector normally starts by believing the paper, because otherwise the certificate would be worthless. Third, because paper can be true and the ship still bad, there is a route for the seafarer himself to raise something: on board first, quietly, to the people who can fix it fastest - and if that fails, to an official ashore who can escalate it right up to the international body itself. And fourth, if what the inspector finds is bad enough, the ship can simply be stopped from sailing.

The idea worth holding onto is the one that connects the middle two. A ship can be fully certified, inspected and lawful on paper while a seafarer sits on board unpaid. Certificates catch systems; they do not catch individual wrongs. The complaint is what closes that gap - which is exactly why a complaint is itself one of the things that entitles an inspector to stop believing the paper and start looking properly.

The last part asks where an Indian seafarer stands. The answer turns on a fact about the trade: most Indian seafarers sail on foreign ships, so India is usually not the flag State and cannot inspect the vessel. What India can reach is the agent who put the man on board - which is why the licensing of crewing agents does more practical work for an Indian seafarer than the flag State machinery ever will.

decomposition_gate.question_intent: Four limbs, four marks each, that together walk the whole of MLC Title 5 and then step outside it into Indian domestic machinery. The examiner is testing whether the candidate knows the ENFORCEMENT architecture, not the welfare provisions. The discriminating judgements are: that the DMLC is split between the competent authority and the shipowner; that the port State's ordinary inspection is a DOCUMENT REVIEW because the certificate is prima facie evidence; that the Convention publishes NO LIST of detainable deficiencies but gives two grounds; and that for most Indian seafarers the operative Indian responsibility is LABOUR-SUPPLYING and not flag State.
decomposition_gate.mark_allocation: 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 = 16, printed against every limb. This is the constraint that shapes the answer. LIMB a) IS THE HARD ONE - flag State and port State responsibilities are two large subjects sharing four marks, and the corpus's own July 2024 question gives exactly that material sixteen. It is therefore written as two tight halves with the certification machinery compressed to essentials. Limbs b), c) and d) each have a natural four-mark shape. The February 2023 sitting of this question printed no marks at all and could distribute by judgement; this one cannot.
decomposition_gate.examiner_expectation: That Title 5's three-way split - flag State, port State, labour-supplying - is known and used. That the on-board and onshore procedures are treated as a connected escalation and not as two unrelated lists. That the candidate knows detention under MLC is reached through a more detailed inspection opened on defined triggers, and rests on two grounds rather than a published list. That limb d) is answered with the Convention's own route first and Indian machinery second, and that no circular number, cell or forum is invented.
decomposition_gate.primary_source_plan: THE MLC IS HELD BY THE TRUE SOURCE CORPUS AT 319524c - the base text, the ILO Compendium 4th revised edition, and the 2022 amendments SEGREGATED in a not-yet-in-force folder. That segregation is doing real work here: it is what allows the 2022 set to be named as adopted-and-not-in-force without risk of it leaking into the operative statement. Regulation and Standard identities and their effects are therefore P1 where they come from the held base text, and P2 where carried through the donor. NO PROVISION IS QUOTED. The Indian limb has no held primary source - the Merchant Shipping Act, 1958 is not held - and is P2 throughout.
decomposition_gate.freshness_risk: HIGH - and the reason is physical rather than theoretical. The corpus holds TWO consolidated texts of this Convention, one carrying the amendments through 2018 and one carrying the 2022 set, and the second is present, readable and INAPPLICABLE at this sitting. That is precisely the circumstance in which a wrong-edition answer gets written without anyone noticing. The operative text here is the Convention AS AMENDED THROUGH THE 2018 SET; the 2022 amendments enter into force 23 December 2024, seventeen months after this sitting, and appear only as adopted-and-not-in-force.
decomposition_gate.jurisdiction_risk: MEDIUM - limb d) is expressly Indian and there is no held Indian primary source. The Merchant Shipping Act, 1958 governs and the maritime administration is DG Shipping; the 2025 Act commenced 15 March 2026, thirty-two months future, and the administration was renamed at that point. Neither appears as operative. No section number, no circular number, no named cell, office, forum or tribunal is asserted anywhere in limb d).
decomposition_gate.technical_ambiguities: The February 2023 sitting of this question prints 'Compliant Procedures'; this sitting prints 'Complaint Procedures' and is the correct one. The answer therefore proceeds directly, with no adjudication paragraph, and the relationship is recorded in question_delta and in the paper anchor rather than shown to the candidate. 'Detainable deficiencies' is port State control vocabulary imported into an MLC question; the answer states the MLC grounds and expressly does not import the Paris MoU list, which is a different regime reaching detention by a different route.
decomposition_gate.target_answer_shape: Seven numbered sections under four single-letter limb headings: one framing section on the edition and the architecture, one section for limb a), TWO for limb b) because the on-board and onshore procedures are separate machinery, one each for limbs c) and d), and a short closing section drawing the thread from limb b) through limb c) to limb d).

quick_revision.major_trap: Answering limb (c) from the Paris MoU. The MLC publishes NO LIST of detainable deficiencies - it gives two grounds, reached only through a more detailed inspection opened on one of four triggers. The second trap is the DMLC split: PART I IS THE COMPETENT AUTHORITY'S and PART II IS THE SHIPOWNER'S, and candidates reverse them. The third is answering limb (d) as though India were the flag State: for most Indian seafarers it is not, and the operative head is labour-supplying responsibility.

retrieval_cards.prompt: The DMLC has two parts. Who draws up each, and what does each contain?
retrieval_cards.answer: Part I is drawn up by the COMPETENT AUTHORITY of the flag State and identifies the national requirements implementing the Convention. Part II is drawn up by the SHIPOWNER and sets out the measures adopted on that ship to ensure ongoing compliance between inspections. Candidates habitually reverse them.

retrieval_cards.prompt: On what grounds may a port State detain a ship under the MLC, and how is that point reached?
retrieval_cards.answer: The Convention publishes no list. Two grounds: conditions clearly hazardous to the safety, health or security of seafarers; or a serious or repeated breach of the requirements, including seafarers' rights. They are reached only through a MORE DETAILED INSPECTION, opened on one of four triggers - documents not produced, not maintained or falsely maintained; clear grounds; the flag changed to avoid compliance; or a complaint.

retrieval_cards.prompt: Trace the onshore complaint-handling procedure from the seafarer to its highest rung.
retrieval_cards.answer: The seafarer complains to an authorized officer in the port. The officer makes an initial investigation and seeks resolution at ship level. If unresolved, he notifies the flag State, seeking advice and a corrective plan of action, copying the shipowners' and seafarers' organisations in the port State. If still unresolved, the report and the flag State's response go to the Director-General of the International Labour Office. The source of the complaint is kept confidential throughout.

retrieval_cards.prompt: Must a seafarer exhaust the on-board complaint procedure before going to anyone else?
retrieval_cards.answer: No. The Convention expresses a preference for resolution at the lowest level, but that preference is expressly WITHOUT PREJUDICE to the seafarer's right to complain directly to the master and directly to external authorities such as the flag State administration or an authorized officer in a port of call. Victimization for filing a complaint is prohibited and must be penalized.

retrieval_cards.prompt: Why must a port State accept the Maritime Labour Certificate and DMLC as prima facie evidence?
retrieval_cards.answer: Because without that presumption the certificate would carry no value and every port would re-audit every ship. The presumption makes the ORDINARY port State inspection a document review, limited to the Articles, the Regulations and Part A of the Code, and it is displaced only when one of the four triggers for a more detailed inspection is present.

retrieval_cards.prompt: Which MLC responsibility is the operative one for most Indian seafarers, and why?
retrieval_cards.answer: LABOUR-SUPPLYING responsibility, the third limb of Title 5. Most Indian seafarers serve on foreign-flag ships, so India is neither flag State nor usually port State and cannot inspect the vessel. What it can reach is the recruitment and placement service that put the seafarer on board - licensing it, requiring registers and verification of employment agreements, enforcing the prohibition on charging recruitment fees, and requiring a system of protection to compensate the seafarer for the agent's failure.

retrieval_cards.prompt: Which text of the MLC is operative at a July 2023 sitting, and what is adopted but not in force?
retrieval_cards.answer: The Convention as amended through the 2018 amendments. The 2014 set (abandonment and financial security), the 2016 set (harassment and bullying) and the 2018 set (wages while held captive) are all in force. The amendments approved by the International Labour Conference at its 110th Session in 2022 are ADOPTED BUT NOT IN FORCE - they enter into force on 23 December 2024, seventeen months after this sitting.

retrieval_cards.prompt: How is the MLC Code amended, and why does it matter?
retrieval_cards.answer: By the ILO's own machinery - the Special Tripartite Committee, with approval by the International Labour Conference - not by IMO tacit acceptance. Candidates habitually import the IMO amendment procedure, which produces a wrong account of how and when a change becomes binding.
